chapter: Follow-up questions, Bird and the Ellington sidemen
title: John Levy's stranded eight-piece band and growl trumpeter Russell Gillam
summary: Before New York, Levy organized an eight-piece band that got stranded, with Russell Gillam as a Cootie-style trumpeter.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: How long did you and John Levy work with Stuff Smith in New York? You got there in '44.
Yeah. Let's see.
And how long did you stay with Stuff?
About a couple of years, that's all.
Uh-huh.
But John and I had worked together before that. I mean with Tony [Fambreau.] And John had organized a little eight piece band, we went out on the road with it.
John Levy did?
Uh-huh.
Oh. That was at what point, before you went to New York or after?
Oh, yeah, way before.
Oh. How long did John have his band?
Well, we got stranded, so it didn't last very long.
(Laughter)
That was the one you got stranded with?
Yeah.
Who all was in it?
Oh, a bunch of local people. Let me see,
who in the heck was in the band? Well, there was a trumpet player that sounded a whole -- he was with Tony Pambreau, but he sounded a whole lot like -- a whole lot like Cootie Williams.
Huh.
His name was Russell Gillam. He's gone now, you know, but he was a very good growl trumpet player. Because we all were crazy about Duke's band, you know. The whole bunch.
